descripcion: At B2 the goal is to disagree politely without attacking the other person's statement directly — the finer grading between partial agreement and clear disagreement (C1) isn't the target yet. Choosing confidently between yes, but and I see it differently is enough.

filas: I agree with you on that.
I see it a bit differently.
I don't really agree with that.

ejemplos.texto: I completely agree with you on that.
Yes, that's true, but I think there's still a problem.
I see it a bit differently, to be honest.

notas: Yes, but is the most common and useful phrase for agreeing while still adding a limit.
I see it a bit differently is more polite than I don't agree and works well for a first disagreement.
Agreeing with emphasis first shows you're listening, even if you plan to disagree afterwards.

contraste.es: Tienes razón corresponds to you're right and sí, pero to yes, but, so the basic formulas transfer. No estoy de acuerdo becomes I don't agree, which is correct but sounds firmer in English than I'm not sure I agree.
contraste.de: Du hast recht is often calqued as you have right; English uses be: you're right. Ja, aber corresponds directly to yes, but.
contraste.it: Sono d'accordo is often calqued as I am agree; English agree is a verb: I agree. Hai ragione similarly leads to you have reason instead of you're right.
contraste.fr: Je suis d'accord is often calqued as I am agree; English agree is a verb: I agree. Tu as raison similarly leads to you have reason instead of you're right.
contraste.pt: Concordo corresponds exactly to I agree, a single verb in both languages. Tens razão, however, leads to you have reason instead of you're right.

errores: Disagreeing directly without acknowledging anything first.
Starting with yes but forgetting the but, leaving the disagreement unclear.
Using the same phrase every time, regardless of the degree of agreement.

autochequeo: Have I acknowledged the other view before disagreeing?
Is the but clearly present after yes?
Does the phrase match the degree of my agreement or disagreement?
Does the disagreement sound polite, not blunt?
Have I used at least two different phrases, not always the same one?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on agreeing and disagreeing. Check whether the right phrase was chosen and whether the disagreement sounds polite. Do not rewrite the text.
